title: Review of the Marangoni swim screen on fresh seed 73: mar 60 against base raises the per-cycle swim of dividing rods (median 1.30 -> 2.04 rod lengths, share >= 2.5 from 0 to 0.20, 2 of 10 reach 3) while keeping 85% of persistent splits
summary: c34's Marangoni world, WORLD_P CARGO 0 (base) and CARGO 0, mar 60, 128^2, 200 frames, seed 73, labkit; per-track traits with c00's extract.py unchanged (D = net / median 4 sqrt(lambda_max), dividing = split-born ending in >= 2 daughters living >= 20 frames). Base: 13 dividing rods, median D 1.30, none >= 2.5 (best 2.34), persistent splits 27, generation 4. mar 60: 10 dividing, median D 2.04, 2 of 10 >= 2.5 and both >= 3 (best 3.47), persistent splits 23, generation 4. Difference in medians +0.75, bootstrap CI [+0.03, +1.55], Mann-Whitney one-sided p 0.016 (compare73.txt). The finding's direction and size replicate on a third seed: raising the Marangoni coefficient lengthens the swim per cycle without stopping division.

observations.M: compare73.txt: dividing rods median D 1.30 (base, n=13) vs 2.04 (mar 60, n=10), share >= 2.5 0 vs 0.20; persistent splits 27 vs 23

seeds_run.result: pass: D +0.75 rod lengths, splits 85% of base

verdicts.limitation: One fresh paired seed with 10-13 dividing rods, so the CI is wide; I did not test mar 80, phi_b or the other screened parameters. D uses the finding's 4 sqrt(lambda_max) rod length, not signed-distance lengths.
